chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Kenny Clarke in Paris: first meeting and a borrowed pay
summary: Collins met Clarke in Cincinnati with Roy and recorded with him in Paris for Nicole Barclay, where Clarke borrowed his pay.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And then when I went to New York we became very good friends, as a matter of fact we played around, we did quite a bit of recording, with different groups. As a matter of fact I

think Kenny did some recording with Mildred Bailey too, during this time. But when I went to Europe I saw Kenny again. This is another time he'd left the -- I think this time he stayed though. No, he didn't either, he came back once again to the states to live. But at that time it was one -- in '47 he had left for good, you know. He got disgusted with America and the Jewish bebop as he called it, and went to Europe. But -- so I did some recording with Kenny over there, and I -- all I know it was for Nicole Barkley. I forget -- I think her label was the Blue Note also, wasn't it, or --
Any way, I did some recording over there because why I remember is because Kenny borrowed the money that I made that day and he never paid me. I got paid for the date and he borrowed it right there.
You and Kenny Clark and whom else was (Inaudible) on the date?

Oh, some of the guys in Howard's group. I forgot who it was. Some -- yeah. But Kenny as I said, Kenny was -- it was his date, I really believe it was his date. But it was for Nicole Barclay Barkley, and she was trying to get Errol to record for her then. I don't think he would, for personal reasons, you know. But he didn't record for her. But I'm sure that we did -- I know that we did some recordings during that time.
